name: Operational Risk Policy
description: A formal policy document defining the bank's stance and framework for managing operational risk, specifically focusing on losses resulting from internal failures or external events.

name: Operational Risk
description: The risk of financial loss resulting from inadequate or failed internal processes, people, and systems, or from external events.
context: Operational Risk = Risk of loss due to inadequate/failed processes, people, systems, or external events.

name: Process Risk Policy
description: A policy governing the identification and mitigation of process failures that cause errors or delays within the bank's operations.
context: Process failures causing errors or delays

name: Process Risk
description: The risk of process failures resulting in operational errors or delays, specifically including account opening, payment processing, reconciliation, and fraud detection failures.
context: Process failures causing errors or delays

name: Standard Operating Procedures
description: The use of standardized operating procedures to mitigate the risk of process failures and errors.

name: Staff Training
description: The provision of training to staff as a mitigation measure against process-related errors and delays.

name: Supervisory Review
description: The implementation of supervisory reviews to oversee processes and mitigate the risk of operational failure.

name: Process Automation
description: The application of automation to banking processes where possible to reduce the likelihood of manual errors.

name: Mandatory Mitigation of Process Risk
description: Requirement to mitigate process failures causing errors or delays through the use of SOPs, training, supervisory review, and automation.

name: System Risk
description: A category of risk involving technology failures that result in service disruption. This includes outages, data corruption, integration failures, and security breaches.

name: System Outages
description: A specific type of technology failure under System Risk that causes service disruption.

name: Data Corruption
description: A specific type of technology failure under System Risk that causes service disruption.

name: Integration Failures
description: A specific type of technology failure under System Risk that causes service disruption.

name: Security Breaches
description: A specific type of technology failure under System Risk that causes service disruption.

name: System Redundancy and Backup
description: An operational safeguard used to mitigate System Risk by ensuring system availability and data recovery.

name: Disaster Recovery Planning
description: A planning mechanism used to mitigate System Risk and ensure service continuity after a failure.

name: Change Management
description: A control process used to mitigate System Risk by managing how changes to technology are implemented.

name: Security Controls
description: General protective tools and mechanisms used to mitigate System Risk and prevent security breaches.

name: People Risk
description: A category of risk encompassing potential losses or failures resulting from staff errors or misconduct within the bank.

name: Unauthorized Transactions
description: A specific risk under People Risk where transactions are executed without proper authorization.

name: Policy Violations
description: A risk involving the failure of staff to adhere to established bank policies.

name: Staff Negligence
description: Risk arising from staff failure to exercise reasonable care in the performance of their duties.

name: Staff Theft and Fraud
description: Risk of internal financial crime where staff engage in theft or fraudulent activities.

name: Training and Awareness
description: An operational safeguard used to mitigate People Risk by ensuring staff are educated and aware of their obligations.

name: Segregation of Duties
description: A control mechanism that divides tasks among multiple people to reduce the risk of error or fraud.

name: Access Controls
description: Technical or operational safeguards that restrict system or physical access to authorized personnel only.

name: Monitoring and Audits
description: The process of ongoing oversight and periodic formal reviews to detect and prevent People Risk.

name: Compliance Risk
description: A category of risk encompassing regulatory violations or breaches, specifically including KYC failures, AML violations, GDPR breaches, and reporting errors.
context: Regulatory violations or breaches: - KYC failures - AML violations - GDPR breaches - Reporting errors

name: KYC Failures
description: A specific type of regulatory violation involving failures in the Know Your Customer verification process.

name: AML Violations
description: A regulatory breach involving violations of Anti-Money Laundering laws and policies.

name: GDPR Breaches
description: A regulatory violation involving breaches of the General Data Protection Regulation.

name: Reporting Errors
description: Regulatory violations resulting from errors in mandatory reporting obligations.

name: Policies and Procedures
description: The implementation of formal policies and procedures used to mitigate compliance risk and regulatory violations.

name: Compliance Training
description: Training programs provided to staff to ensure adherence to regulations and mitigate compliance risk.

name: Regular Audits
description: The performance of periodic audits to detect and mitigate regulatory violations and compliance failures.

name: Regulatory Monitoring
description: The ongoing process of monitoring regulatory changes and compliance status to mitigate risk.

name: General Data Protection Regulation
description: The data protection regulation the bank must comply with to avoid GDPR breaches.

name: Fraud Risk Policy
description: The governing policy section addressing the identification and mitigation of internal and external fraud risks within FirstUK Bank.

name: Customer Fraud
description: Fraud committed by or against customers, specifically characterized by unauthorized transactions.

name: Employee Fraud
description: Internal fraud committed by bank staff, specifically characterized by embezzlement.

name: Third-party Fraud
description: Fraud involving external partners or vendors.

name: System Fraud
description: Fraud involving the manipulation of bank data or systems.

name: Fraud Detection Systems
description: Technical systems implemented to detect fraudulent activity.

name: Segregation of Duties
description: An operational safeguard ensuring that no single individual has control over all phases of a business transaction to prevent fraud.

name: Whistleblower Procedures
description: Formal procedures allowing for the reporting of suspected fraudulent activity.

name: Investigation Protocols
description: Standardized protocols for conducting investigations into suspected fraud.

name: Reputational Risk
description: The risk of reputational damage resulting from operational failures, regulatory breaches, or misconduct. This risk is characterized by negative public perception arising from customer complaints, press coverage of violations, or service disruptions.

name: Customer Complaint Risk
description: A specific driver of reputational damage stemming from customer complaints, particularly those amplified via social media.

name: Regulatory Violation Risk
description: The risk of reputational damage caused by regulatory violations that become public through press coverage.

name: System Outage Risk
description: The risk of reputational damage resulting from system outages and the subsequent disruption of services.

name: Fraud and Misconduct Risk
description: The risk of reputational damage and public scandal arising from internal or external fraud and misconduct.

name: Service Quality Focus
description: An operational focus on maintaining service quality to mitigate the risk of customer complaints and reputational damage.

name: Regulatory Compliance Monitoring
description: The implementation of regulatory compliance measures to prevent violations that could lead to negative press and reputational harm.

name: Incident Response
description: The use of incident response protocols to manage and mitigate the impact of system outages or other failures.

name: Media Management
description: The application of media management strategies to control the bank's public image during crises or scandals.

name: External Risk
description: Risks arising from external events beyond the bank's control, including environmental, technical, third-party, and legal shifts.

name: Natural Disasters
description: A specific category of external risk involving natural events that may disrupt bank operations.

name: Cyberattacks
description: External threats involving malicious digital attacks against the bank's infrastructure.

name: Vendor Failures
description: Risks associated with the failure of third-party service providers to meet their obligations.

name: Regulatory Changes
description: Risks stemming from changes in the external regulatory environment that may impact bank operations.

name: Business Continuity Planning
description: The operational safeguard used to mitigate the impact of external events and ensure the bank can continue functioning during disasters.

name: Cybersecurity Measures
description: Technical and operational safeguards implemented to protect the bank from cyberattacks.

name: Vendor Management
description: The process of monitoring and managing third-party providers to mitigate the risk of vendor failure.

name: Regulatory Monitoring
description: The ongoing process of tracking regulatory changes to ensure the bank remains compliant.

name: Risk Assessment Framework
description: A governing framework establishing the processes for identifying, logging, and assessing risks within the bank. It mandates a continuous approach to risk identification and the maintenance of a centralized risk register.

name: Mandatory Annual Departmental Risk Assessment
description: A requirement for each department to conduct a risk assessment on an annual basis as part of the continuous risk identification process.

name: Management Process Walk-throughs
description: An obligation to perform process walk-throughs with management to identify potential risks.

name: Incident Trend Analysis Requirement
description: A requirement to analyze trends in incidents to identify emerging or systemic risks.

name: Regulatory Change Assessment
description: An obligation to assess changes in regulations to determine their impact on the bank's risk profile.

name: External Threat Monitoring
description: A requirement to monitor external threats as part of the continuous risk identification process.

name: Centralized Risk Register
description: A centralized log used to document identified risks, including their description, impact, likelihood, and risk ratings (current and residual), as well as the assigned responsible party.

name: Responsible Party
description: The individual or entity designated within the Risk Register as being accountable for a specific identified risk.

name: Risk Scoring Policy
description: A formal framework defining the methodology for assessing risk through impact and likelihood scales. It establishes a risk rating matrix to categorize risks from Low to Critical based on financial loss and frequency.

name: Risk Impact Assessment Requirement
description: Mandates the use of a 1–5 scale to determine the impact of a risk, correlating the score to specific loss amounts ranging from <£10k (Minimal) to >£1M (Critical).

name: Risk Likelihood Assessment Requirement
description: Mandates the use of a 1–5 scale to determine the likelihood of a risk occurrence, based on frequency ranging from 'Rare' (<1 in 10 years) to 'Very Likely' (Monthly+).

name: Risk Rating Categorization and Action Mandate
description: Defines the required response based on the calculated risk score: Green (1-5) requires standard controls, Yellow (6-10) requires monitoring, Orange (12-15) requires senior oversight, and Red (16-25) requires immediate mitigation.
context: Green (1–5): Low risk, accept, standard controls
Yellow (6–10): Medium risk, monitor, targeted controls
Orange (12–15): High risk, mitigate, senior oversight
Red (16–25): Critical, urgent action, immediate mitigation

name: Operational Risk
description: Risks associated with system outages, process errors, and service disruptions as defined in the likelihood and impact scales.

name: Regulatory and Compliance Risk
description: Risks involving regulatory breaches and threats to the bank's operating license.
context: Major breach, large loss, license risk

name: Fraud Risk
description: Risks associated with fraud detection events, categorized as 'Likely' in the frequency scale.

name: Standard Controls
description: Baseline safeguards applied to risks categorized as Green (Low risk).
context: Green (1–5): Low risk, accept, standard controls

name: Targeted Controls
description: Specific monitoring mechanisms applied to risks categorized as Yellow (Medium risk).
context: Yellow (6–10): Medium risk, monitor, targeted controls

name: Senior Oversight
description: Management-level supervision required for risks categorized as Orange (High risk).
context: Orange (12–15): High risk, mitigate, senior oversight

name: Immediate Mitigation
description: Urgent corrective actions required for risks categorized as Red (Critical).
context: Red (16–25): Critical, urgent action, immediate mitigation

name: Risk Assessment Process
description: A formal framework defining the four-step lifecycle for identifying, scoring, mitigating, and monitoring risks within the bank. It establishes a collaborative workflow between individual departments and the Risk Team.

name: Mandatory Risk Identification
description: Requires departments to lead the identification of potential risks, specifically assessing process failures, systems, and fraud scenarios.
context: Assess process failures, systems, fraud scenarios

name: Risk Scoring and Residual Risk Calculation
description: Mandates a joint effort between the Risk Team and the Department to estimate impact and likelihood, account for existing controls, and calculate the resulting residual risk.

name: Risk Mitigation and Control Implementation
description: Obligates departments to identify control gaps, implement targeted controls, and assign a specific responsibility and timeline for mitigation.

name: Continuous Risk Monitoring and Escalation
description: Requires continuous monitoring of key risk indicators (KRIs), the adjustment of controls as necessary, and the escalation of risks if they increase.

name: Fraud Scenarios
description: Potential fraud-related events that must be identified and assessed as part of the department-led risk identification process.
context: Assess process failures, systems, fraud scenarios

name: Process Failures
description: Risks arising from failures in internal processes that must be identified during the risk assessment process.
context: Assess process failures, systems, fraud scenarios

name: System Risks
description: Risks associated with bank systems that are subject to identification and assessment by departments.
context: Assess process failures, systems, fraud scenarios

name: Key Risk Indicators (KRIs)
description: Monitoring mechanisms used to continuously track risk levels and trigger control adjustments or escalations.

name: Department
description: The organizational unit responsible for leading risk identification, implementing targeted controls, and assigning mitigation timelines.

name: Risk Team
description: The specialized team that collaborates with departments to score risks, estimate impact/likelihood, and calculate residual risk.

name: Control Framework
description: The governing framework establishing the Three Lines of Defense model to manage risk, monitoring, and assurance within the bank.

name: Frontline Management
description: The first line of defense consisting of department heads responsible for risk, operating procedures, daily monitoring, and immediate incident response.

name: Risk & Compliance
description: The second line of defense responsible for the risk policy and framework, independent risk monitoring, control testing, and escalation procedures.

name: Internal Audit
description: The third line of defense providing independent assurance through control testing, audit reports, and follow-up verification.

name: Daily Monitoring
description: A first-line operational safeguard involving the daily monitoring of activities to identify risks.

name: Immediate Incident Response
description: A first-line control requiring the immediate response to identified incidents.

name: Independent Risk Monitoring
description: A second-line control providing independent oversight and monitoring of risk.

name: Control Testing
description: A control mechanism utilized by both the second line (Risk & Compliance) and third line (Internal Audit) to verify the effectiveness of controls.

name: Escalation Procedures
description: A second-line operational mechanism for escalating risks and compliance issues.

name: Independent Assurance
description: A third-line safeguard providing objective assurance on the bank's risk management processes.

name: Audit Reports
description: The formal documentation of audit findings produced by the third line of defense.

name: Follow-up Verification
description: A third-line control to ensure that audit findings and recommendations have been addressed.

name: Incident Management Policy
description: A formal policy governing the management of unplanned events that result in actual loss or regulatory breaches within FirstUK Bank.

name: Incident Risk
description: An unplanned event that causes an actual financial loss or a regulatory breach.
context: Incident = Unplanned event causing actual loss or regulatory breach

name: Incident Reporting Policy
description: A formal policy governing the immediate actions, escalation paths, and data capture requirements following an operational incident.

name: Immediate Manager Notification
description: A mandatory requirement for staff to report an incident to their manager immediately upon discovery.

name: Mandatory Incident Logging
description: An obligation to ensure that all incidents are formally recorded within the designated incident log.

name: Financial Loss Escalation Threshold
description: A mandatory escalation requirement to the Risk team for any incident resulting in a loss exceeding £10,000.
context: Escalate to Risk team if >£10k loss

name: Regulatory Breach Escalation
description: A mandatory requirement to escalate the incident to the Compliance department if a regulatory breach has occurred.
context: Escalate to Compliance if regulatory breach

name: Incident Information Capture Standard
description: A standard defining the specific data points that must be captured for every incident, including date, time, type, affected systems, impact, root cause, and containment steps.

name: Incident Log
description: The operational tool used to record and track incidents as required by the reporting policy.

name: Manager
description: The first point of contact for incident reporting who receives immediate notifications from staff.

name: Risk Team
description: The body responsible for handling escalated incidents involving financial losses greater than £10,000.
context: Escalate to Risk team if >£10k loss

name: Compliance
description: The department responsible for managing and overseeing incidents that constitute a regulatory breach.
context: Escalate to Compliance if regulatory breach

name: Financial Loss
description: The risk of monetary loss resulting from an incident, with a specific reporting threshold of £10,000.
context: Escalate to Risk team if >£10k loss

name: Regulatory Breach
description: The risk of failing to comply with external laws or regulations, triggering a mandatory escalation to Compliance.
context: Escalate to Compliance if regulatory breach

name: Fraud Investigation Policy
description: A policy governing the investigation of fraud incidents, specifying mandatory timelines for completion based on the financial value of the incident and the required elements of the investigation report.

name: Investigation Timeline for Incidents under £10k
description: Mandatory requirement that fraud incidents with a value of less than £10,000 must be investigated within 5 business days.

name: Investigation Timeline for Incidents between £10k and £100k
description: Mandatory requirement that fraud incidents with a value between £10,000 and £100,000 must be investigated within 2 business days.

name: Immediate Escalation for Incidents over £100k
description: Mandatory requirement for immediate escalation to the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) for any fraud incident exceeding £100,000.
context: Incidents >£100k: Immediate escalation to CRO + CEO

name: Mandatory Investigation Elements
description: Requirement that all fraud investigations must include a detailed timeline of events, root cause analysis, lessons learned, corrective action, and prevention measures.

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: Executive role responsible for receiving immediate escalations regarding high-value fraud incidents exceeding £100,000.

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: Executive role responsible for receiving immediate escalations regarding high-value fraud incidents exceeding £100,000.

name: Root Cause Analysis
description: An operational mechanism used during fraud investigations to identify the underlying cause of an incident to prevent recurrence.

name: Incident Escalation Policy
description: A policy governing the triggers, timelines, and reporting lines for escalating financial losses based on the amount of the loss.

name: Low Value Loss Reporting Requirement
description: For losses under £1,000, the Department Manager is required to report the incident to Risk.

name: Medium Value Loss Reporting Requirement
description: For losses between £1,000 and £10,000, the Risk Manager must report the incident to the CRO within 1 day.
context: £1k–£10k | Risk Manager | Report to CRO within 1 day

name: High Value Loss Reporting Requirement
description: For losses between £10,000 and £100,000, the CRO and CEO must be notified within 24 hours.

name: Critical Value Loss Reporting Requirement
description: For losses exceeding £100,000, immediate notification to the Board and Regulators is mandatory, including formal regulatory notification.

name: Department Manager
description: Responsible for reporting losses of less than £1,000 to the Risk function.

name: Risk Manager
description: Responsible for reporting losses between £1,000 and £10,000 to the CRO within a one-day timeframe.
context: £1k–£10k | Risk Manager | Report to CRO within 1 day

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: An executive role that receives reports for medium-value losses and is part of the escalation chain for high-value losses (£10k–£100k).

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: An executive role required to be notified of losses between £10,000 and £100,000 within 24 hours.

name: Board
description: The governing body that must be notified immediately in the event of losses exceeding £100,000.

name: Regulators
description: External authorities that must receive immediate notification for losses exceeding £100,000.

name: Financial Loss
description: The risk of financial loss, categorized by monetary thresholds to determine the appropriate escalation path.

name: Incident Escalation Matrix
description: A structured matrix used to ensure that financial losses are reported to the correct level of management within specified timeframes.

name: Key Risk Indicators
description: Early warning signals used by the bank to identify and monitor emerging risks before they materialize into significant events.
context: KRIs = Early warning signals of emerging risk

name: Operational Risk Policy
description: A policy governing operational risk management through the definition of Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), target thresholds, and mandatory remediation actions when targets are exceeded.

name: Operational Risk
description: The overarching risk category addressed by the monitoring of account opening errors, system availability, reconciliation variances, and compliance violations.

name: Fraud Risk
description: The risk of fraudulent activity, monitored via the fraud detection rate KRI to ensure gaps are investigated and rules are tuned.

name: Compliance Risk
description: The risk of regulatory or policy violations, with a target of zero occurrences and a requirement for immediate remediation.

name: Remediation of Account Opening Errors
description: Mandatory requirement to review the process and retrain staff if account opening errors exceed a target of 0.5%.
context: Account opening errors | <0.5% | Review process, retrain staff

name: System Availability Remediation
description: Obligation to investigate outages and remediate issues if system availability falls below the 99.8% target.

name: Reconciliation Variance Correction
description: Requirement to investigate and correct daily reconciliation variances that exceed £1,000.

name: Fraud Detection Rule Tuning
description: Obligation to tune fraud rules and investigate gaps if the fraud detection rate falls below 97%.
context: Fraud detection rate | 97%+ | Tune fraud rules, investigate gaps

name: Immediate Remediation of Compliance Violations
description: Strict requirement for immediate remediation upon the occurrence of any compliance violations (target is 0).

name: Customer Complaint Root Cause Analysis
description: Requirement to perform a root cause analysis if customer complaints exceed 2 per 1,000 accounts.
context: Customer complaints | <2 per 1,000 accounts | Root cause analysis

name: Operational KRI Monitoring
description: The use of Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) to monitor operational health across account opening, system availability, reconciliation, fraud, compliance, and complaints.

name: Staff
description: Staff members who are subject to retraining in the event that account opening error targets are exceeded.

name: Process KRI Policy
description: A policy governing the Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) for core banking processes, defining target thresholds and monitoring frequencies for operational performance.

name: Account Opening Error Rate Threshold
description: Requirement to maintain an error rate of less than 0.5% for the Account Opening process, with monitoring conducted on a monthly basis.

name: Payment Processing Failure Rate Threshold
description: Requirement to maintain a failed transaction rate of less than 0.1% for Payment Processing, with monitoring conducted on a daily basis.

name: Fraud Detection False Positive Rate Threshold
description: Requirement to maintain a false positive rate of less than 2% for Fraud Detection, with monitoring conducted on a weekly basis.
context: Fraud Detection | False positive rate | <2% | Weekly

name: AML Screening Delay Threshold
description: Requirement to ensure AML Screening delays remain under 2 hours, with monitoring conducted continuously.
context: AML Screening | Screening delay | <2 hours | Continuous

name: Operational Risk
description: The risk of loss resulting from inadequate or failed internal processes, people, and systems, as evidenced by the tracking of error rates and processing failures.

name: Fraud Risk
description: The risk of fraudulent activity, mitigated by monitoring the false positive rate of detection systems.

name: Money Laundering Risk
description: The risk of money laundering, mitigated by ensuring timely AML screening.

name: KRI Monitoring
description: The operational mechanism of tracking Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) on daily, weekly, monthly, and continuous schedules to ensure process stability.

name: AML Screening Process

name: Account Opening Process
description: The process of opening new accounts, monitored for error rates to ensure operational quality.

name: Quarterly Risk Committee Meeting Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement for the Board Risk Committee to convene and review risk governance matters on a quarterly frequency.

description: A designated member of the Board Risk Committee responsible for risk oversight.

description: A designated member of the Board Risk Committee responsible for risk oversight.

description: A designated member of the Board Risk Committee responsible for risk oversight.
context: Members: CRO, CEO, CFO, Compliance Head, Internal Audit

name: Department Risk Owners
description: Staff members responsible for the identification, implementation, and monitoring of risks and controls within their specific departmental areas, including reporting to the Risk team and escalating incidents.

name: KRI Monitoring
description: The process of monitoring Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) as part of the risk management obligations of Department Risk Owners.

name: Incident Escalation
description: The operational requirement to escalate identified incidents to the appropriate authority.

name: Risk Identification Obligation
description: A mandatory requirement for Department Risk Owners to identify risks within their specific area of responsibility.

name: Control Implementation Requirement
description: A mandatory requirement for Department Risk Owners to implement necessary controls to mitigate identified risks.

name: Risk Reporting Obligation
description: A mandatory requirement for Department Risk Owners to report risk-related information to the Risk team.

name: Risk Team
description: An internal team responsible for the maintenance of the risk framework, aggregation of risk assessments, and monitoring of trends. They serve as the regulatory liaison and are tasked with reporting findings to the Board Risk Committee.

name: Board Risk Committee
description: The governing body to which the Risk Team reports risk assessments and trend monitoring.

name: FirstUK Bank Risk Appetite Statement
description: A governing statement defining FirstUK Bank's overall risk appetite as conservative and establishing specific quantitative tolerances for operational losses, incidents, compliance, and fraud.

name: Operational Risk
description: The risk of loss resulting from inadequate or failed internal processes, people, and systems, with a defined annual loss tolerance of less than £50k.

name: Compliance Risk
description: The risk of legal or regulatory sanctions, financial loss, or reputation loss resulting from failure to comply with laws and regulations, for which the bank has zero tolerance.

name: Fraud Risk
description: The risk of financial loss due to fraudulent activity, with an annual loss tolerance threshold of less than £100k.

name: Annual Operational Loss Limit
description: A requirement that annual operational losses must be kept below £50,000, which represents 0.15% of revenue.

name: Major Incident Frequency Limit
description: A requirement that the bank must experience fewer than one major incident per year.

name: Zero Tolerance for Compliance Violations
description: A strict prohibition against compliance violations, stating that zero violations are tolerated.

name: Annual Fraud Loss Limit
description: A requirement that total annual losses resulting from fraud must be less than £100,000.

name: Training & Awareness Policy
description: A policy governing the training and awareness requirements for staff regarding operational risk. It defines mandatory training frequencies and levels based on staff roles.

name: Mandatory Annual Operational Risk Awareness Training for All Staff
description: A mandatory requirement for all staff members to complete a 1-hour operational risk awareness training session on an annual basis.

name: Quarterly Risk Workshops for Process Owners
description: A mandatory requirement for process owners to participate in risk workshops on a quarterly basis.

name: Advanced Training and Certifications for Risk Team
description: A requirement for members of the risk team to undergo advanced training and obtain professional certifications.

name: Operational Risk
description: The category of risk that the training and awareness program is designed to mitigate through staff education.

name: Staff Training

name: All Staff
description: The collective of all bank employees who are obligated to complete annual operational risk awareness training.

name: Process Owners
description: Staff members responsible for specific business processes who are required to attend quarterly risk workshops.

name: Risk Team

name: Audit & Monitoring Policy
description: A governing framework defining the requirements for internal and regulatory audit activities to ensure operational risk management and compliance.

name: Annual Operational Risk Assessment
description: A mandatory requirement to conduct an operational risk assessment on an annual basis as part of the internal audit process.

name: Process Control Testing
description: An obligation to perform testing on process controls to ensure they are operating effectively.

name: KRI Validation
description: A requirement to validate Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) to ensure accurate risk measurement and reporting.

name: Incident Investigation Sampling
description: A requirement to perform sampling of incident investigations to verify the quality and thoroughness of the process.

name: PRA Periodic Operational Risk Reviews
description: A requirement to undergo periodic operational risk reviews conducted by the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA).

name: Compliance with Pillar 2 Requirements
description: An obligation to ensure the bank complies with the specific regulatory requirements defined under Pillar 2.

name: Prudential Regulation Authority
description: The regulatory body responsible for conducting periodic operational risk reviews of the bank.

name: Pillar 2 Requirements
description: The specific regulatory framework and requirements that the bank must comply with regarding capital and risk management.

name: Operational Risk
description: The risk of loss resulting from inadequate or failed internal processes, people, and systems, which is the primary focus of the audit and monitoring activities.

name: Internal Audit
description: The overarching internal mechanism used to perform risk assessments, control testing, and KRI validation.

name: Regulatory Audit
description: The external monitoring mechanism involving reviews by the PRA to ensure regulatory compliance.

name: Risk Department
description: The organisational department responsible for risk oversight and the management of related documentation.

name: Business Continuity Plan
description: A formal governing document outlining the bank's strategy and procedures for maintaining business operations during a disruption.

name: Risk Assessment Template
description: A standardised tool used by the bank to ensure consistent identification and evaluation of risks.

name: Incident Log
description: A tracking mechanism used to record and monitor incidents for compliance and operational oversight.
